title: Scope and Closure Bug

bugs.explanation: Using `var` in a `for` loop creates a single shared `i` variable. All closures capture the same reference; by the time they run, `i === 5`. Use `let` to create a new binding per iteration.

title: this Context Lost in Callback

bugs.explanation: A regular `function` callback gets its own `this` binding. Inside `setInterval`, `this` is `undefined` (strict mode) or `globalThis`, not the Timer instance. Use an arrow function, which inherits `this` from the enclosing method.

title: Accidental Global Variable

bugs.explanation: Assigning to `count` without declaring it with `let`/`const`/`var` creates an implicit global variable (in sloppy mode). In strict mode it throws `ReferenceError`. Always use `let` or `const` to declare variables.

title: Overwriting Built-in
code:
const undefined = 42;
console.log(undefined);

bugs.fix:
// Never shadow built-in identifiers like undefined, null, NaN, Infinity
const myValue = 42;
bugs.explanation: Shadowing `undefined` with a local variable is legal JavaScript but dangerous — in that scope, `undefined` no longer refers to the primitive and type checks like `x === undefined` break. Never shadow built-in identifiers.

Implicit Return in Arrow Function
code:
const double = x => { x * 2; };
console.log(double(5));

bugs.explanation: Arrow functions with a block body `{ }` require an explicit `return`. Without it, the function returns `undefined`. Either add `return x * 2` inside the braces, or use a concise body (no braces) for implicit return.

title: Object Shorthand Method vs Property
Unexpected Semicolon Insertion

bugs.explanation: ASI (Automatic Semicolon Insertion) inserts a semicolon after `return` when the next token is on a new line. The function returns `undefined`, not the object. Put the opening brace on the same line as `return`.

title: Array Holes
delete Array Element Creates Hole

bugs.explanation: `delete arr[1]` removes the value but leaves a hole — the array length stays at 3 and `arr[1]` becomes `undefined`. Use `splice(1, 1)` to properly remove the element and update the length.

eval Is Dangerous
code:
const expr = '2 + 2';
console.log(eval(expr));

bugs.explanation: `eval()` executes arbitrary code in the current scope, creating security vulnerabilities (XSS, code injection) and preventing engine optimizations. Avoid `eval`. If dynamic evaluation is genuinely required, use `new Function()` which runs in a separate scope.

Class Not Hoisted

bugs.explanation: Unlike function declarations, `class` declarations are not hoisted into an initializable state. Accessing a class before its declaration throws `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'Point' before initialization` due to the TDZ. Always declare classes before use.
